newsitem.title: BULGARIA: EBRD TO BUY 20 PCT IN BULGARIA'S FIRST INV BANK.
newsitem.headline: EBRD TO BUY 20 PCT IN BULGARIA'S FIRST INV BANK.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank licensed on Thursday the acquisition of a 20 percent stake in the private First Investment Bank (FIB) by the European Bank for Development and Reconstruction (EBRD).
"The BNB licensed the EBRD to acquire up to 20 percent of voting shares and up to 20 percent of non-voting shares in the capital of FIB," the BNB said in a statement.

The EBRD board approved two days ago subsciption to 20 percent of newly issued shares of FIB capital at aggregate subscription price not exceeding 5.2 million European Currency Units ($6 million), the EBRD said.

The project aims to increase FIB funding resources and further improve its capital adequacy, develop its loan portfolio and "encourage international banks to open up their lending exposure limits to FIB and to Bulgarian banks in general," said an EBRD statement.
FIB was set up in 1993 as fully private with the objective to become a full-service corporate bank catering to the emerging private sector in Bulgaria.
The bank posted 2.28 billion lev gross profit for 1996 which was fully set aside as provision against its risk assets.

In April FIB shareholders decided to raise capital to five billion levs from 2.2 billion levs now in line with expected rise of BNB minimum capital requirements. FIB's capital to risk assets ratio was 15.16 percent at end-1996.

BNB's licensing coincides with the first day of the new reformist cabinet in office. Bulgaria's Prime Minister Ivan Kostov, appointed by parliament on Wednesday, pledged to speed up reform and boost foreign investment.

EBRD revised its funding strategy for Bulgaria last year after delayed reforms, a weak and poorly functioning banking system, corruption and slow and reluctant privatisation deterred development of the private sector.

The EBRD has so far approved 21 investments totalling 215.5 million Ecu in the financial sector, agribusiness, transportation, telecommunications, energy insurance and consumer goods. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
